verifier_notes.method: Every source_url in R03.json was re-fetched independently on 2026-08-05. help.sap.com/doc/<docset>/<ver>/en-US/<guid>.html legacy routes render for WebFetch. help.sap.com/docs/** SPA routes are JS-gated for WebFetch and were rendered with the in-app browser (preview_start/navigate/get_page_text), which returned full verbatim prose. learning.sap.com/courses/** rendered for WebFetch. No source was verified from memory or plausibility.
verifier_notes.gap_closed: R03.json listed page 30cb8deab95e4d8c9420aeabb2ae496f (S/4HANA Cloud 'Budget Availability Control' root) as uncapturable due to an SPA race. The verifier captured it successfully. It confirms 'the budget availability control calculates the available budget' but still prints NO explicit available-budget formula, so R03's negative result on the formula STANDS and is now independently corroborated.

results.what_source_actually_says: Page 'Assigned Values for Projects' (Project System (PS), Version 2025 FPS01 Feb 2026) opens verbatim: 'The assigned value for projects is calculated from:' followed by a nine-item list.
results.notes: Anchor record for the whole lane. Confirmed at the current PS documentation version.

results.what_source_actually_says: Bullet 1: 'Actual costs of WBS element carrying budget'.
Bullet 2: 'Statistical actual costs of WBS element carrying budget'.
Bullet 3: 'Actual costs of subordinate WBS elements if these do not carry budget'.
results.notes: The 'only when subordinates do not carry budget' conditional is verbatim, not an interpretation.

results.what_source_actually_says: Bullet 5: 'Commitments of WBS element carrying budget'.
results.notes: Source lists commitments as a component; it does not itself narrate the 'consume budget before actual cost posts' consequence, but that follows directly and is corroborated by R03-088 (error-type limit blocks PO/PR postings).

results.what_source_actually_says: Bullet 6: 'Commitments of subordinate WBS elements if these do not carry budget'.

Bullet 7 verbatim: 'Maximum of plan and actual costs + commitments from assigned networks or orders', followed by an IMG pointer to Project System > Costs > Planned Costs > Define Order Value Updating for Orders for Projects.
results.notes: CONFIRMED and important. The MAX (not SUM) rule is real and is the single most non-obvious element of the formula. Note the IMG pointer: order value updating is itself configurable, so the MAX rule's inputs are config-dependent.

results.what_source_actually_says: Bullet 8: 'Debit from settlement to WBS element'.
Bullet 9: 'Credit from settlement to budget-controlled object (internal order, WBS element)'.
results.notes: The claim's reading (credits reduce assigned value only for budget-controlled receivers) is corroborated by the mirror exclusion at R03-013.

results.what_source_actually_says: Under a 'Caution' admonition: 'Not used for calculation of the assigned value:' followed by four items.
results.notes: The exclusion list is inside a Caution block, supporting the record's 'normative, not incidental' framing.

results.what_source_actually_says: Exclusion 1 verbatim, with IMG pointer 'Project System > Costs > Budget > Specify Exempt Cost Elements'.
results.notes: Config carve-out confirmed, including the exact IMG path.

results.what_source_actually_says: Exclusion 2 verbatim, plus: 'This can happen if you have not defined ++ as a business transaction group in Customizing for tolerance limits.' IMG pointer: Project System > Costs > Budget > Define Tolerance Limits.
results.notes: IMPORTANT SIDE-EFFECT the record does not surface: failing to define the ++ catch-all transaction group causes costs to silently DROP OUT of assigned value entirely. That is a silent under-consumption failure mode, not merely a missing tolerance check.

results.what_source_actually_says: Exclusion 3: 'Credits from settlement to an object that is not budget-controlled (for example, cost center)'.
results.notes: Confirms the asymmetry: settling to a cost center does NOT free project budget.

results.what_source_actually_says: Exclusion 4 is the single word 'Revenues'.
results.notes: Quote is a single word but is a discrete list item, so the match is genuine. The claim's generalisation ('budget consumption in SAP PS is a cost-side concept only') is a fair reading of a bare exclusion entry.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Assigned Value: Total of commitment and actual postings. The assigned value is only displayed if availability control is active.'
results.notes: QUOTE CONFIRMED BUT READ THE WARNING. This compact definition CONFLICTS in scope with the authoritative definition at R03-001..R03-009. It omits (a) the MAX(plan, actual+commitment) rule for assigned networks/orders, (b) settlement debits, (c) settlement credits, (d) statistical actual costs. Implementing 'assigned = commitments + actuals' literally will UNDERSTATE assigned value and let projects overspend. The Budget Value Display page is a UI field glossary, not the calculation spec. See contradictions[0].

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Original budget that was changed by budget updates (supplements, returns, and transfers).'

'Distributed Value: The total of the current budget (see below) for a WBS element or lower-level WBS elements. The distributed values can be displayed only in the controlling area and object currencies.'
results.notes: Quote matched verbatim including the '(see below)' cross-reference. SAP's own phrasing 'for a WBS element or lower-level WBS elements' is ambiguous; the claim's reading (budget held by children) is the correct one and is confirmed by R03-036 and R03-018. Also note the currency restriction in the second sentence, which the record omits: distributed values display ONLY in controlling-area and object currencies.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'This is the difference between the current budget and distributed value.'

'Cumulated value: Total of the annual budgets. The system determines the cumulated value always using only the values in the currency that you are currently using for processing the budget.' and 'Remaining value: Difference between overall budget and cumulated.'
results.notes: Both halves of the claim confirmed. Extra unrecorded constraint: cumulated is computed only in the currency currently being used to process the budget.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Release: Based on the released budget from the current budget'.

Full sentence: 'Note that after budget updates are made by supplements, returns, and transfers, the displayed values (such as the distributed value) are always based on the current budget, not the original budget.'
results.notes: Record quoted the trailing clause; the full sentence confirms the claim exactly.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'In the budget profile, you use Activation Type to define whether, and how, availability control is to be activated.'

'There are three different activation types: 0 = Cannot be activated / 1 = Automatic Activation With Budget Allocation / 2 = Background Activation'. Followed by: 'If you chose background activation, you can activate Online Availability Control for a specific project.'
results.notes: 'Exactly three' confirmed by SAP's own 'three different activation types'. Note online activation is a rider on type 2, not a fourth type — consistent with R03-030.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Determination of WBS elements carrying budget ("controlling elements")' — the first of three activation activities.
'It checks the assigned funds against the controlling element budgets. The assigned funds can be on the budget-carrying WBS element, the lower-level WBS elements and their assigned project orders.'
results.notes: Defines the three-way scope of the check. This is the scope rule the Zoho rollup must replicate.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'After activation, each posting to the project is checked by the availability control.'
results.notes: Source says every posting is checked. It does NOT use the word 'synchronous'; the record's 'synchronous gate' gloss is an inference, though a reasonable one given R03-041/R03-088 (postings are rejected).

results.what_source_actually_says: Full sentence: 'As availability control affects system performance, you should activate it in the background for projects with less detail, only when you think that the budget may be exceeded.'
results.notes: Quote matched as a prefix, but the record TRUNCATES the sentence before ', only when you think that the budget may be exceeded.' The dropped clause is material: SAP's recommendation is conditional on suspecting overspend, not a blanket recommendation for low-detail projects.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Background activation for availability control checks whether or not the usage level defined in the budget profile has been reached.'
results.notes: Confirms a usage-level threshold exists. Consistent with R03.json's own gap note that the field's numeric semantics/default are undocumented on any fetched page — the verifier found no such definition either.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Background activation of availability control logs the objects for which you activated availability control.'
'You can activate availability control for a project before the usage level is reached or before the next batch run.'
'Availability control is activated the next time you choose Save or Check. After activation, every posting in the project is checked by the availability control.'
results.notes: Record quote is an exact prefix of the full text.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'In the budget profile you determine whether/how availability control is to be activated and which budget values should be checked by availability control.'
'You can decide whether availability control is carried out on the basis of year-independent (= total values) or year-dependent values.'
results.notes: Confirmed, but see R03-113 notes: the same page shows the check basis has a THIRD dimension (currency) the record never captures.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Overview of funds, their assignment and type' appears under the Passive Availability Control heading; 'Prevents the assignment of too many funds' appears under Active Availability Control.
results.notes: The passive/active split claimed by the record is confirmed by the page's own heading structure.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Prevents the assignment of too many funds' under Active Availability Control.
'The budget from the controlling element that is not yet distributed to other, lower-level WBS elements.' — the page's definition of Distributable Budget.
results.notes: Underscores in the record's quote are markdown-emphasis artefacts around 'not'; the underlying wording matches.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'control costs actively by issuing warnings and error messages when costs are incurred' — in the Use section.

Quote verbatim: 'You can define relative or absolute variance from budget values as tolerance limits for budget profile/transaction group/action combinations.' BUT the page is FUNDS MANAGEMENT documentation — its action list reads 'Warning with Mail to funds center manager', and 'funds center' is Funds Management master data with no Project System equivalent.
results.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: in SAP Funds Management, tolerance limits are keyed on budget profile / transaction group / action and may be relative or absolute. The record presents this as generic SAP tolerance grammar feeding a Project System budget design without any module caveat. R03.json's own gaps list admits the PS-specific 'Define Tolerance Limits' IMG page was never reached. PS does have its own Define Tolerance Limits activity (IMG path confirmed on the assigned-values page at R03-012), so the grammar is plausibly shared — but that is unproven from this source.

results.what_source_actually_says: Quote verbatim: 'If no tolerance limit is found, the posting is permitted.' Same Funds Management page as R03-038.
results.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: in Funds Management availability control, a posting for which no tolerance limit is found is permitted. HIGH-STAKES OVERSTATEMENT: the record generalises this into 'the control is opt-in and fails open, not closed' as a design principle for the whole budget-availability build. Fail-open is a control-design decision that must not rest on a cross-module inference. It IS indirectly corroborated for PS by R03-012 (undefined ++ transaction group causes costs to be excluded from assigned value), which points the same way — but that is corroboration, not proof. Confirm against the PS 'Define Tolerance Limits' IMG page before relying on fail-open.

results.what_source_actually_says: Quote verbatim: 'The system informs you that the tolerance limit is being exceeded. However, the posting in question is not rejected.' Page title 'Availability Control Actions'; module confirmed as Funds Management.
results.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: Funds Management action 1 warns without rejecting. The numeric action codes 1/2/3 are Funds Management artefacts as evidenced here. The SUBSTANCE is independently corroborated Tier-1 and PS-side by R03-087 (warning-type limit still allows budget use), so the behaviour is safe to design against; the 'action 1/2/3' numbering is not proven to be PS terminology from this source.

results.what_source_actually_says: Quote verbatim: 'If a posting leads to the action 3 tolerance limit being exceeded, the system rejects the posting and generates an error message.' Funds Management page.
results.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: Funds Management action 3 rejects the posting with an error. Substance corroborated PS-side by R03-088 (error-type limit blocks purchase orders/requisitions). Same module-scope caveat as R03-040.

results.what_source_actually_says: The action list reads exactly: 'Warning' / 'Warning with Mail to funds center manager' / 'Error message'.
results.notes: CONFIRMED because this record is the only one in the tolerance cluster that explicitly states its Funds Management scope in claim_text. Note the notification target is a FUNDS CENTER manager (FM master data). The PS analogue is the WBS-element/project-definition manager per R03-096 — a different field on a different object. Do not conflate them.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'All business transactions are assigned to a transaction group in availability control.'
'This general transaction group simplifies entry and is useful if you do not want to define separate tolerance limits for every transaction group.'
results.notes: Quote matched as a substring. CAVEAT: the claim's second clause — 'specific groups override the catch-all' — is NOT stated on this page. That precedence rule is separately and properly evidenced by R03-090 (S/4HANA Cloud), which is CONFIRMED, so the design assumption holds; it just does not come from this source.

results.replacement_quote: During the project, it is possible that the budget may be reduced, even though assigned funds already exist in the project. You require this transaction group to enable availability control to take into any account retrospective budget changes.
results.what_source_actually_says: The page does not contain the record's condensed string 'Budgeting: Enables availability control to account for retrospective budget changes during projects'. It states the fuller sentence given as replacement_quote.
results.notes: Claim substance CONFIRMED; original evidence_quote was a paraphrase, not verbatim. The real wording is stronger and more useful: it names the specific scenario of budget being REDUCED while assigned funds already exist — the retrospective-reduction edge case the Zoho design must handle.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'You can exclude a WBS element with budget and the lower-level account assignment elements from availability control.'

Full sentence: 'If a WBS element has this status, then the assigned funds are not included in the availability control, in other words, no action is triggered. However, the assigned values are still updated on the controlling element.'
results.notes: Record quote matched. Design-critical and correctly captured: exclusion suppresses the ACTION but not the ACCOUNTING. Assigned value keeps accruing while the gate is off.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Budget allocation for a project or an order is generally preceded by a cost plan that provides the initial basis for determination and allocation of the budget.'
results.notes: Record quote is an exact prefix.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The budget is the approved cost framework for a project. It differs from the cost plan in that it is binding.' — quote matched verbatim on SAP's own learning site.
results.notes: SOURCE TIER GATE. Tier 2 vendor-learning may reach CONFIRMED for behaviour/UX only. This record is claim_class ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLE — a definitional/normative statement, not behaviour — so it cannot exceed UNVERIFIED under the gate. The quote genuinely matched and the source is SAP-owned; the binding-vs-indicative distinction is also directionally corroborated by Tier-1 R03-048. Treat as sound but cite a Tier-1 page if the blueprint leans on 'binding' as a legal/accounting characterisation.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Select the WBS elements that contain the plan values you want to use as the budget.' The percentage step is also present: 'Enter the percentage of the plan total and decide whether the value is to Overwrite the existing value [or] Be added to the existing value.'
results.notes: Both halves of the claim confirmed. Overwrite-vs-add is an extra option the record does not mention and which matters for repeated plan-to-budget transfers.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The period of time during which budgeting is allowed'.
Verbatim: 'Whether budgeting is allowed for total annual values, and/or annual values'.
results.notes: Quote matched EXACTLY, including SAP's apparent typo 'total annual values' where 'total values' is meant. The record's claim_text silently normalises this to 'total values, annual values, or both'. That reading is almost certainly right (and is consistent with R03-033 and R03-117) but note the blueprint is relying on a corrected reading of a malformed source line.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'You can allocate budget after the status Created has been reached.'
'The Receiver year is the year in which the receiver object receives additional budget.'
'If you select this indicator, the system changes the total budget for the receiver to the same extent as the annual values.'
results.notes: Record quote is an exact substring.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'You can use the checking function before posting to determine whether the entered items contain any errors.' plus 'Any rows containing errors found by the system are not posted.'
results.notes: Both halves of the claim (check-before-post, erroneous rows excluded) confirmed verbatim.

results.what_source_actually_says: Step 3 of the procedure: 'Enter the returns entering the sender WBS element and the amount. If the template does not specify sender years, select the year and, if required, the option to include total values.'
results.notes: Record quote matched as a substring.

results.what_source_actually_says: Full list: 'Transfers between different WBS elements in the same period. The sender and the recipient cannot belong to the same subtree. Transfers between the same WBS element in different periods (also recourse or carryforward). Transfers between different WBS elements in different years'.
results.notes: CONFIRMED. UNRECORDED CONSTRAINT the lane missed: 'The sender and the recipient cannot belong to the same subtree.' That is a hard structural validation rule on budget transfers and should be added to the blueprint's transfer validation.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The system only includes budget items in the relevant object currency in the Entered Budget. Transfers made in other currencies are not displayed as an entered value in objects from higher hierarchy levels. The system includes all budget items in the current budget.'
results.notes: Confirmed including the claim's 'though current budget includes them' clause, which the surrounding sentence supports explicitly.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The Check function executes both consistency checks and availability control checks.'
'the system checks whether the budget values of a lower-level of the WBS element (distributed values) exceed the budget value of the level above.'
results.notes: Record quote matched as a substring. Confirms distributed <= parent budget as an enforced consistency rule.

results.what_source_actually_says: Full sentence: 'Even if the total values match the annual values in a defined currency, the values in the controlling area or object currency can differ (if the exchange rate type or the entered value date for the total values is different from that for the annual values).'
results.notes: Record truncates before the parenthetical, which names the actual CAUSE: differing exchange rate type or value date between total and annual values. Worth carrying into the design — it is not generic rounding drift.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Distribute the total budget (using the top-down method) to the individual elements in the work breakdown structure.'
results.notes: Record quote is an exact prefix.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Reassigning a WBS element (that has a budget) within the work breakdown structure is not supported.'
results.notes: Corroborated independently by R03-068 (budgeted status blocks reassignment).

results.what_source_actually_says: 'At the same time, the system overwrites a budget value on a WBS element with the distributed value (roll-up).'
results.notes: Record quote matched as a substring. Note 'overwrites' — this is destructive to the parent's own entered budget.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If budgeting is decentralized (budgeting upwards or bottom-up), the person responsible for the overall budget requires an overview of the sectional budgets.'
results.notes: Record quote matched as a substring; full sentence also confirms Total Up is the bottom-up counterpart to top-down distribution.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'After you allocate budget to a WBS element for the first time, the system status budgeted is set.'
results.notes: Quote matched. CAVEAT on claim_text: 'persists even if the budget is later removed' is only conditionally true — R03-069 gives two conditions under which the status IS removed. State it as 'persists unless budget is zeroed via the same transaction that allocated it'.

results.what_source_actually_says: Prohibited activities list: 'Deletion of WBS elements' and 'Reassignment of WBS elements and all subordinate objects'.
results.notes: Record quote is one of two list items; the claim's second half is confirmed by the second item.

results.what_source_actually_says: Two conditions, both required: 'The budget is removed using the same transaction with which it was allocated' and 'The selected WBS elements have budget 0'.
results.notes: Record concatenates the two list items with 'and'; both present and both required.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Each change that you save in budgeting is documented as a line item by the system.'
'You can prohibit line item writing for changes to the original budget by means of a user status, although the system continues to write line items for budget updates.'
results.notes: Both halves of the claim confirmed in one sentence.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Each budget line item is saved in the currency in which you entered it (budgeting currency).'
'Keep the exchange rates as stable as possible. In particular, you should not change the exchange rates while entering the original budget.'
results.notes: Quote matched. The 'because retranslation distorts comparisons' rationale in claim_text is the record's own gloss, not source wording.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The budget carryforward enables you to carry forward budget remainders from projects, internal orders, and plant maintenance orders to the following fiscal year.'
'A budget that has not been used up is mainly defined here as the difference between planned budget and incurred actual costs.'
results.notes: CONFIRMED and design-critical, exactly as the record flags: carryforward uses planned budget MINUS ACTUAL COSTS, which is a DIFFERENT base from assigned value (assigned value includes commitments, settlement debits and the order MAX rule). Note SAP's own hedge 'mainly defined here'.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Commitments are not taken into account when the unused budget is calculated. Therefore you need to carry forward commitment before you do so for the budget.'
results.notes: Both the exclusion and the sequencing requirement are confirmed in adjacent sentences.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'There is no availability control during the budget carryforward.'
results.notes: Confirmed. The carryforward run is exempt from the gate.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Budget carryforward is only allowed if the object (WBS element/internal order) has been Created, Released, or Technically completed.'
results.notes: The three permitted statuses are verbatim. The claim's 'blocked for Closed or deletion-flagged objects' is the logical complement of 'only allowed if', not separately quoted wording.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'You cannot carry forward negative budget into the following year.'

'You can carry forward budget more than once in a row. Each time, budgets are carried forward that were not included in the previous runs, because the corresponding internal orders or WBS elements were locked, for example.'
results.notes: Repeatability confirmed. NOTE: the claim's word 'idempotent' is the record's gloss and is imprecise — SAP describes repeat runs as picking up PREVIOUSLY EXCLUDED budgets, which is a top-up semantic, not idempotence. The 'test and update modes' half of the claim was not located in the fetched text; treat that sub-clause as unevidenced.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If you make follow-up postings of actual costs, the system posts back budget that was carried forward to the following year (a maximum of the total budget carried forward to the following year).'
results.notes: Both the reversal behaviour and the cap are confirmed, the cap verbatim in the parenthetical.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Here, you specify the time range of the budget, the cost items (as relevant semantic tags), the tolerance limits for budget usage, and the requested system response.' Configuration activity ID 102413. Documentation version: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608 Latest.
results.notes: Confirmed at the current Cloud release.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The Time Range defines whether the budget is considered as a yearly budget or an overall budget for projects and WBS elements.'
'If you select Overall Budget, the posted costs are compared with the overall budget of a project, which could span more than one fiscal year.'
'If you select Annual Budget, the posted costs are compared with the annual budget of a project within the related fiscal year.'

'The Tolerance Limits for the budget usage rates are maintained for each activity group. When you define a budget tolerance limit, you also assign a message type to it, which alerts the user when the tolerance limit has been reached. You can decide whether these message types are warnings or errors.'
results.notes: Both halves of the claim confirmed. This is the PS-relevant modern replacement for the Funds Management action model at R03-040/041 — and it has only TWO message types (warning, error), no 'warning with mail' tier.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If you assign a warning to a budget tolerance limit, the budget can still be used even after the tolerance limit has been exceeded.'
results.notes: Strongest PS-side Tier-1 evidence that warnings are advisory. Use this rather than the Funds Management action-1 page.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If this tolerance limit is exceeded, the system responds with an error message and commitments, such as purchase orders or purchase requisitions, can't be posted.'
results.notes: Matched (source uses a typographic apostrophe in 'can't'). Strongest PS-side Tier-1 evidence that errors block. Note the blocked objects named are COMMITMENTS (PO/PR) specifically.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'In a budget availability control profile, the activity group All Activity Groups (++) is mandatory. You must configure at least one of the following: All Activity Groups (++) with a warning message type or All Activity Groups (++) with an error message type.'
results.notes: Confirmed including the warning-or-error requirement. Other activity groups (Purchase Requisition 01, Purchase Order 02) are explicitly optional.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'If you've assigned the Purchase Order (02) activity group to your budget availability control profile and you create a purchase order, the usage rate in the tolerance limit for activity group Purchase Order (02) is checked. Otherwise, the usage rate for activity group All Activity Groups (++) is used by default.'
results.notes: This is the source that properly establishes specific-overrides-catch-all precedence (cf. note on R03-044).

results.what_source_actually_says: 'For each semantic tag, you can specify budget usage rates at which a first notification and further notifications are sent.'
results.notes: Note the constraint the record omits: 'For each profile you can only assign one semantic tag' and 'It isn't possible to change the semantic tag in an existing budget availability control profile.' That is a real design constraint on a one-tag-per-profile model.

results.what_source_actually_says: Field names appear verbatim as list items: '% of Budget Used before First Notification' and '% Increment for Further Notifications', under situation template EPPM_PROJBUDGETTHRESHOLDEXCEEDED.
results.notes: Confirmed. Useful extra: the notification mechanism is a Situation Template surfaced in the Project Budget Report app, not an email action.

results.what_source_actually_says: The quote is verbatim but sits inside a CAUTION admonition that reads in full: 'The Project Budget Report app (ID: F3377) doesn't display data related to semantic tag PSQBUDGET. To display data related to PSQBUDGET, use the Project Financial Booklet Enterprise app (ID: F8698) which correctly displays the Budget, Project Stock, Actual Cost, Commitment, Assigned Value, and Available Budget in Global Currency.'
results.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: ONE specific app (Project Financial Booklet Enterprise, F8698) displays those six measures in Global Currency, and it is named only as the workaround for a limitation of the default Project Budget Report app (F3377) with the PSQBUDGET balance-sheet semantic tag. The record generalises this into 'SAP's project financial reporting surfaces ... as distinct displayed measures'. The six-measure list is real and useful as a reporting model, but it is not a general statement about SAP project reporting, and the Global Currency qualifier is app-specific.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'You can select either Global Currency or Project Currency. However, you must ensure that budget data is available in the currency type that you select. If you select Project Currency, ensure that Project Currency is maintained in the projects to which you want to assign the Budget Availability Control Profile.'
results.notes: Confirmed, with an extra prerequisite the record omits (Project Currency must be maintained on the project master).

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The budget availability control starts with the budget maintenance process, runs with each commitment posting and actual cost posting, and ends with the analysis of costs and budget.'
'No manager name has been entered in the WBS element, or in the project definition.'
results.notes: Matched apart from sentence-initial capitalisation. Confirms the PS notification target is the WBS-element/project-definition manager — distinct from Funds Management's funds center manager (cf. R03-042).

results.replacement_quote: Availability control is not active, or the tolerance limits have not yet been exceeded.
results.what_source_actually_says: The page does NOT contain the record's string 'This indicates availability control isn't active or tolerance limits haven't been exceeded.' It states the sentence given as replacement_quote.
results.notes: Claim substance CONFIRMED (silence is ambiguous between 'not active' and 'no limit breached'). The recorded evidence_quote was reworded — different sentence structure and contractions SAP does not use in this page. Replace it.

results.replacement_quote: You can compare the relevant budget and assigned values for a selected quantity of WBS elements in real time.
results.what_source_actually_says: Page title 'Monitor Availability Control for WBS Elements'. Contains 'or call transaction IM_AVCHANA_WBS.' and the opening sentence given as replacement_quote. The record's quote 'drill down according to the characteristics in this layout' does appear, in 'If a layout is already active, you can drill down according to the characteristics in this layout.'
results.notes: Unusual case: the original evidence_quote MATCHES the page but is IRRELEVANT to the claim — it evidences layout drill-down, not the claimed real-time budget-vs-assigned comparison or the transaction code. Both claimed facts are nonetheless true and now properly evidenced. Swap in the replacement quote; the transaction code is separately supported by 'or call transaction IM_AVCHANA_WBS.'

results.what_source_actually_says: 'You can plan the cost of each WBS element on a yearly basis or plan using the overall value.'
'Projects can be planned in the controlling area currency, object currency, or transaction currency and you can configure the currency type using the planning profile.'
results.notes: Both the three currencies and the planning-profile control are in one sentence.

results.what_source_actually_says: The page states only: 'The first time you run cost planning for a project, this automatically creates version 0.' It contains NO statement that version 0 is the leading (or operative) plan version.
results.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: the first cost planning run for a project automatically creates version 0. The claim's appended assertion 'which is the leading plan version' is not supported by this source. R03-102's page refers to 'the leading CO version' but never equates it with version 0. If the blueprint needs version 0 == leading version, source it separately.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Transferring ECP from an appropriation request to a project or WBS element always occurs in the leading CO version.'

'You can use cost element planning when you have detailed information available, normally at a more advanced stage of a project.' and separately 'Overall planning is the simplest type of cost planning.'
results.notes: Both halves of the claim confirmed; the quoted fragment correctly attaches to cost element planning.

'Structure planning is neither by cost element nor is it period-specific.'
results.notes: Tier-2 permitted to reach CONFIRMED for behaviour/characteristics of the planning method. Minor referent drift: the source says 'Structure planning'; the record says 'Structure-oriented overall planning'. Treat as the same method (corroborated by Tier-1 R03-120, which lists 'Structure planning value (independent of cost element)').

results.notes: Tier-2 CONFIRMED as a behaviour statement, and independently corroborated Tier-1 by R03-025 ('It checks the assigned funds against the controlling element budgets').

results.notes: SOURCE TIER GATE: Tier-2 vendor-learning cannot confirm a claim classed ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLE (behaviour/UX only). The substance is nonetheless corroborated by Tier-1 R03-061, which shows the consistency rule is machine-enforced by the Check function. Cite R03-061 in the blueprint instead of this record.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'In many organizations, distributing a budget is not the same as releasing the funds allocated to it.' Page title 'Budget Releases'; module confirmed as Funds Management / Budget Control System.
results.notes: CONFIRMED as a generic organisational principle — SAP itself frames it with 'In many organizations', so it is not a product-behaviour claim being over-generalised. SCOPE FLAG: unlike its sibling R03-110, this record's claim_text does NOT disclose that the page is Funds Management/BCS rather than Project System. Add that caveat. That PS separately supports a released-budget layer is evidenced by R03-020 and R03-115.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'A release is based on the current total budget, which you can release at one time. You can also release your budget periodically.' Module: Funds Management / Budget Control System.
results.notes: CONFIRMED including the record's own explicit Funds Management scope caveat, which the verifier independently corroborated. Do not present this as PS behaviour.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Their only purposes are planning and budget monitoring. Therefore, debits that are not eligible for capitalization (internal activity allocation), but that you wish to have reflected in the statistical budget, require special treatment.' The page also confirms no settlement is possible for statistical orders/WBS elements.
results.notes: Record quote is a short fragment but appears verbatim; the surrounding sentence plus the no-settlement statement support the full claim.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'The system provides a passive availability check, which you carry out using reports. In addition, there is an active availability check, which enables you to prevent posting of transactions that would exceed the budget. The system checks the budget when certain transactions are entered. It determines if the available project budget or the available released budget is still sufficient. The system uses tolerance limits you entered in Customizing when making the availability check. In order to use the active availability check, you must enter it in the budget profiles of the statistical order or WBS element.'
results.notes: CONFIRMED, and this passage is more valuable than the record makes out — see R03-113. It contains the closest first-party statement to an available-budget concept: 'It determines if the available project budget or the available released budget is still sufficient.' Note also 'when certain transactions are entered', which qualifies the every-posting framing at R03-026.

results.replacement_quote: It determines if the available project budget or the available released budget is still sufficient.
results.what_source_actually_says: The cited quote ('whether/how availability control is to be activated and which budget values should be checked by availability control') matches verbatim but establishes only that a check basis is configurable — it does not state any subtraction. The same page enumerates EIGHT possible check bases: 'Current overall budget in controlling area currency', 'Current overall budget in object currency', 'Current annual budget in controlling area currency', 'Current annual budget in object currency', 'Released overall budget in controlling area currency (only for projects)', 'Released overall budget in object currency (only for projects)', 'Released annual budget in controlling area currency (only for projects)', 'Released annual budget in object currency (only for projects)'.
results.notes: THE SINGLE MOST LOAD-BEARING RECORD IN THE LANE AND IT REMAINS UNSOURCED. The verifier independently re-ran the search and additionally captured the S/4HANA Cloud 'Budget Availability Control' root page (30cb8dea...) that R03.json could not capture; it says only 'the budget availability control calculates the available budget' and prints no formula. R03's negative result therefore STANDS and is now double-confirmed. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD: (1) the closest first-party wording is on a DIFFERENT page than the one cited — see replacement_quote from fd3dde531ed3424de10000000a174cb4, which names 'available project budget' and 'available released budget' as the quantities tested for sufficiency; cite that instead. (2) The record's parenthetical '(current or released, overall or annual)' MISSES A THIRD DIMENSION: the check basis is also currency-scoped (controlling area vs object currency), giving 2x2x2 = 8 bases, not 4. For a multi-currency Zoho build that omission is material.

results.what_source_actually_says: The page lists, as the constituents of the current budget: 'Original Budget', 'Supplement', 'Return', 'Repostings from the Budget'.
results.notes: All four terms present as consecutive list items, so the quote matches. CAVEAT consistent with the record's own INFERENCE class: SAP prints them as a LIST WITHOUT ARITHMETIC OPERATORS. The '+ supplement, - return, + repostings' sign convention is the record's inference. It is corroborated in direction by Tier-1 R03-016 ('Original budget that was changed by budget updates (supplements, returns, and transfers)') but the signs themselves are not printed anywhere.

results.replacement_quote: Released overall budget in controlling area currency (only for projects)
results.what_source_actually_says: The page does NOT contain the record's string 'For projects: can check against current or released budget'. It expresses the same fact as four separate check-basis entries each tagged '(only for projects)': released overall budget in controlling area currency, released overall budget in object currency, released annual budget in controlling area currency, released annual budget in object currency.
results.notes: Claim substance CONFIRMED — checking against released budget is genuinely project-only. The recorded evidence_quote was a hand-written summary, not source text. Note the released basis is itself split across overall/annual and controlling-area/object currency, so 'released budget' is four configurations, not one.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'You can allocate your budget on the top-down principle or the bottom-up principle.' Page is the Funds Management 'Budgeting and Availability Control' overview.
results.notes: CONFIRMED. Scope note: the page is Funds Management, but the same both-directions capability is independently established for PS by Tier-1 R03-063 (top-down distribution) and R03-065/066 (bottom-up Total Up), so the design conclusion is safe.

results.what_source_actually_says: Full sentence: 'You can allocate overall budgets or annual budgets. You can only allocate an overall budget if you are using a fund.' The fragment 'overall budgets or annual budgets' matches, but the sentence is a disjunction carrying a Funds Management restriction ('a fund' is FM master data). Nothing on this page says the two coexist.
results.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: SAP Funds Management lets you allocate overall budgets or annual budgets, and an overall budget only when using a fund. The record's added clause 'the two coexist rather than being alternatives' is NOT supported here — the source reads as an either/or with a precondition. Coexistence of total and annual layers IS separately evidenced for PS by R03-019 (cumulated vs remaining reconciliation), R03-052 and R03-055 ('Total values too' indicator syncing both layers). Re-anchor the coexistence claim on those PS records and drop this FM page as its evidence.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Instead of specifying the annual values for a certain WBS element using the annual overview, you can also budget all WBS elements for a certain year.'
results.notes: The 'instead of' construction confirms both axes of the claim (per-element-across-years vs per-year-across-elements).

results.notes: Exact match. SAP's word is 'reevaluate'; the record's claim_text says 'revaluate' but its evidence_quote is correct.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'Structure planning value (independent of cost element) + Cost element planning value + Unit costing value + Value of the additive orders for a project, meaning the orders assigned to this and all lower-level WBS elements. ( = Overall planning value that is cost element independent + Value of cost element planning + Unit costing values) + Value of the additive networks and network activities that are assigned to this and all lower-level WBS elements. ( = Plan costs of the networks or activities) = Plan total'
results.notes: CONFIRMED with explicit '+' operators and a terminating '= Plan total'. NOTE THE CONTRAST WITH ASSIGNED VALUE: SAP prints the arithmetic for Plan total but NOT for assigned value or available budget. That asymmetry is itself evidence that the available-budget formula at R03-113 is genuinely absent from the documentation rather than merely unfound.

contradictions.severity: HIGH - internal inconsistency between two Tier-1 SAP pages
contradictions.finding: SAP publishes TWO different definitions of assigned value and the lane records both without reconciling them. The Budget Value Display page (0213d553...) defines Assigned Value as 'Total of commitment and actual postings.' The authoritative Assigned Values for Projects page (f711d553...) defines it as a nine-component aggregate that ALSO includes statistical actual costs, settlement debits, settlement credits to budget-controlled objects, and the MAXIMUM of plan versus actual+commitment for assigned networks/orders.
contradictions.why_it_matters: Both quotes verified verbatim, so neither record is wrong on its own terms — but they are not interchangeable. Building the Zoho availability check on the compact 'commitments + actuals' definition would systematically UNDERSTATE consumption and permit overspend, because it omits the order MAX rule and settlement debits entirely. The compact line is a UI field glossary entry; the nine-component list is the calculation specification. The blueprint must state explicitly which one it implements.
contradictions.verifier_recommendation: Treat f711d553 (R03-001..R03-009) as normative. Demote R03-015 to a UI-label note and annotate it as incomplete.

contradictions.severity: MEDIUM - missing component in the lane's own formula
contradictions.finding: The re-fetched Assigned Values for Projects page lists NINE 'calculated from' components. R03.json records only EIGHT. The missing bullet is: 'Statistical actual costs of subordinate WBS elements if these do not carry budget'. The lane captured the statistical-cost bullet for the budget-carrying element (R03-003) and the actual-cost bullet for subordinates (R03-004) but not the intersection of the two.
contradictions.why_it_matters: If the blueprint's assigned-value formula is assembled from the lane's records alone, it will omit statistical actual costs rolled up from non-budget-carrying children — an under-count in exactly the hierarchy-rollup path the design depends on.
contradictions.verifier_recommendation: Add a record for the ninth bullet before the formula is transcribed into the design.

contradictions.severity: MEDIUM - cross-module scope leakage into the tolerance design
contradictions.finding: Nine records in this lane are sourced from SAP FUNDS MANAGEMENT / Budget Control System pages, not Project System pages. Confirmed by module markers in the re-fetched text: 'Warning with Mail to funds center manager' (9814c753), 'Availability Control Actions' documented under Funds Management (d4f8cc53), 'You can only allocate an overall budget if you are using a fund' (7ef7cc53), and the Budget Releases page (33eacc53). Only R03-042 and R03-110 disclose this in their claim_text.
contradictions.why_it_matters: The most consequential leak is R03-039, 'If no tolerance limit is found, the posting is permitted' — a FAIL-OPEN default being imported into the core control design from a different SAP module. R03.json's own gaps list admits the PS-specific 'Define Tolerance Limits' IMG page was never reached, so PS's actual no-limit-found behaviour is unproven.
contradictions.verifier_recommendation: Prefer the PS-specific S/4HANA Cloud evidence (R03-086/087/088/089/090) for all warning-versus-error tolerance semantics — it is Tier-1, project-scoped, and says the same thing about warnings and errors. Do not ship fail-open as a design principle until it is confirmed against a Project System source.

contradictions.severity: MEDIUM - the load-bearing formula is still not sourced
contradictions.finding: No SAP page prints an explicit 'Available Budget = X - Y' formula. The verifier independently re-searched and additionally captured the S/4HANA Cloud 'Budget Availability Control' root page that R03.json flagged as uncapturable; it states only that 'the budget availability control calculates the available budget'. Separately, the check basis is richer than recorded: the budget-profile page enumerates EIGHT bases (current/released x overall/annual x controlling-area/object currency), whereas R03-113 describes only four.
contradictions.why_it_matters: The entire budget-availability design rests on a formula SAP never states, assembled from two pages. That is defensible only if it is labelled as an inference in the deliverable — which R03-113 does. But the missing currency dimension is a genuine defect: an eight-way check basis has direct consequences for a multi-currency Zoho implementation.
contradictions.verifier_recommendation: Keep R03-113 as INFERENCE, never as SAP-STANDARD. Re-cite it against fd3dde531ed3424de10000000a174cb4 ('It determines if the available project budget or the available released budget is still sufficient'), which is the closest first-party wording and sits on a different page than the one currently cited. Add the currency dimension.

contradictions.severity: LOW - unrecorded hard constraints found during re-fetch
contradictions.finding: Three enforceable constraints appear in the re-fetched sources but are absent from the lane records: (a) budget transfers — 'The sender and the recipient cannot belong to the same subtree.'; (b) assigned value — failing to define '++' as a business transaction group causes costs to be excluded from assigned value entirely, a silent under-consumption failure mode; (c) modern BAC profiles — 'For each profile you can only assign one semantic tag' and the semantic tag cannot be changed once the profile exists.
contradictions.why_it_matters: Each is a validation rule or a modelling constraint the Zoho design would otherwise miss.
contradictions.verifier_recommendation: Add all three to the design constraints section.

summary.most_important_finding: SAP publishes two non-equivalent definitions of assigned value on two Tier-1 pages, and the lane records both without reconciling them (R03-015 vs R03-001..009). The compact 'total of commitment and actual postings' omits the MAX(plan, actual+commitment) rule for assigned orders, settlement debits/credits, and statistical costs. Implementing it would understate budget consumption and permit overspend. Additionally the lane's assigned-value formula is missing one of SAP's nine components.
summary.lane_quality_assessment: R03 is a strong, honestly-sourced lane. Zero contradictions, zero fetch failures, no Tier-3 contamination, and the two hardest calls (no printed available-budget formula; Funds Management pages are not Project System) were both self-flagged in the lane's own gaps section. The defects found are of three kinds: four evidence_quotes that were paraphrased rather than copied (R03-045, R03-097, R03-098, R03-115), seven claims whose text reaches slightly beyond what the cited page supports (R03-038/039/040/041/093/101/117), and the unreconciled assigned-value definitions. None of these invalidate the lane; all are correctable in place.
